articles.title: Lula scores an epic victory in Brazil
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: Brazilian progressive leader and incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva made history last night, defeating far-right Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party in the second round after coming in second in the first round. The results were awaited with bated breath after a judge ordered polls to be open for two more hours following complaints from voters who claimed they had been unable to reach polling places due to transportation problems. First the Workers’ Party (PT), and then the Liberal Party (PL), requested the extension, which paused the vote count until 7:00 pm in Brasília, the capital. articles.title: Student List defeats Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: On October 25, an election list formed after two years of student-led protests in Serbia toppled Aleksandar Vučić and the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). The announcement was met with street celebrations that continued throughout the night, recognizing the outcome as a chance to break with 12 years of the former president’s anti-people policies. Election turnout surged to almost 70% of registered voters. The Student List secured roughly 53% of the vote and the SNS came in second with close to 39%. articles.title: ECOWAS and AES open talks to rebuild relations
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) have opened talks to establish a framework for cooperation, marking a new attempt to rebuild relations following years of political tensions over sovereignty, military coups, and regional sanctions. The two blocs held their inaugural ministerial dialogue in Dakar, Senegal, on October 17, 2026, where they agreed to establish joint thematic working groups to develop a Cooperation Framework Agreement. The meeting brought together representatives of ECOWAS and the AES Confederation, comprising Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger. articles.title: A victory for the Brazilian people once more through Lula
articles.author: Vijay Prashad
articles.content_excerpt: The week before October 25 in Brazil was frenetic. It appeared that every one of the over 200 million Brazilians had a political opinion about the presidential election. The country was fundamentally polarized. Polls showed that the vote was going to be tight, with most polls favoring the challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, and the standard bearer of the far right of a special type. But the incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known as Lula and president of Brazil from 2003 to 2011 and then since 2023, would not allow the polls to stop him. articles.title: No to abolition
articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: Editorial note: The following is a letter response to Hazel W.’s piece, “ In Defense of Abolition .” In July, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) amended its program to call for “abolishing the police and prison system.” Taken literally, that is a mistake. Society needs institutions to patrol and isolate the dangerous few. Even the most radical socialist societies understood this. For example, the Paris Commune — that libertarian-left experiment — had a prefecture of police. articles.title: Lula Draws Hundreds of Thousands in São Paulo for Final Campaign Rally Ahead of Brazilian Elections
articles.content_excerpt: The final campaign rally for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva filled Paulista Avenue in São Paulo this Saturday afternoon, September 24. It was filled with emotion and a strong commitment to defending democracy. By noon, two hours before the official start of the gathering, Paulista Avenue was already a sea of ​​red. It was interspersed with Brazilian flags, LGBTQ+ pride flags, and banners representing grassroots movements, political parties, student organizations, and even soccer clubs. In the crowd were entire families and people of all ages, beliefs, ethnicities, and regions. Some traveled all night to reach São Paulo. articles.title: Serbia’s Student-Led Movement Ousts Strongman Aleksander Vučić in Shock Election Result
articles.content_excerpt: Serbia’s longtime leader Aleksander Vučić has been swept out of power by a historic student-led opposition movement against Vučić’s right-wing Serbian Progressive Party. Candidates from the Student List, who are not students themselves but largely first-time politicians selected by student-led popular assemblies, won a majority of seats in Sunday’s parliamentary elections, marking a seismic shift in Serbian politics. Their victory comes two years into a student-led movement sparked by the collapse of a roof at a train station in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 people. articles.title: Hundreds Protest at Meta Headquarters in Brazil Against Far-Right Bias
articles.content_excerpt: Manifestantes usaram faixas, cartazes e bonecos para denunciar a atuação da Meta nas eleições | Crédito: Igor Carvalho/Brasil de Fato Protesters targeted the multinational corporation Meta, on Monday, October 19, in Itaim Bibi, a neighborhood in São Paulo. Meta owns WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook. According to the organizers, roughly 500 people showed up to protest in front of Meta’s headquarters in São Paulo. Those in attendance criticized Meta’s biased interference ahead of the Brazilian elections. “We cannot claim to have fair elections when a company uses its economic, technical, and technological power to tip the scales in public opinion, which is exactly what is happening,” said Dani Silva, executive director of Ctrl+Z, one of the organizations behind the demonstration.
